items.title: Four killed in helicopter crash in Rio de Janeiro
items.summary: RIO DE JANEIRO: Four people were killed in a helicopter crash Saturday in Rio de Janeiro, including three Colombian tourists from the same family, the country's consul told AFP. The helicopter went down in Tijuca National Park, a mountainside forest with very dense vegetation. Diana Paez, the Consul General of Colombia in Rio de Janeiro, told AFP the three women were part of a family group who had traveled to the Brazilian city to celebrate a girl's 15th birthday.

items.title: Deputy CM: Kundasang's rapid growth was uncontrolled
items.summary: Deputy Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Joachim Gunsalam said the area, which was home to just 500 people and a handful of buildings in the 1970s, underwent rapid change after attracting farmers drawn by its temperate climate and, later, tourism. He also said many landowners gradually built accommodation for visitors as tourism flourished, often without proper planning processes. People simply built another structure on their land for that purpose," he said.

items.title: Heavy rain brings fear to residents
items.summary: RANAU: Whenever heavy rain hits Kundasang here, Stefyanie Myla keeps her 11-year-old daughter home from school. "On days like that, I choose not to send her to school for safety reasons," she said, adding that teachers at SK Don Bosco, Bundu Tuhan, shared the parents' concerns. Stefyanie said that during severe weather, the school allowed students to arrive later until conditions improved.

items.title: Kundasang's beauty under threat [WATCH]
items.summary: However, the growing risk of landslides threatens its appeal. The department's director, Dr Frederick Francis Tating, said rapid development and the expansion of agriculture onto steep, unstable hillsides between 2008 and 2024 had compromised the area. Frederick said Kundasang is vulnerable to landslides because much of the area sits on loose and porous gravel deposits, crushed rock along geological faults and clay-rich rock that weakens when saturated with water.

items.title: Penang woodcarver keeps age-old craft alive as demand grows (VIDEO)
items.summary: The 63-year-old proprietor of Sung Dynasty Wood Carving learned the traditional craft from his late uncle, who had operated from Air Itam, before eventually taking over the trade. Labour of love Lee said he had initially resisted entering the labour-intensive trade when he was younger, choosing instead to work in other industries. Lee Chee Cheng showing the traditional Chinese name stamps that he also makes.

items.title: Hamas says still ready to go ahead with Gaza plan
items.summary: GAZA CITY: Hamas said on Saturday it remained ready to proceed with a US-backed Gaza peace plan and urged pressure on Israel, which insists it did not agree to the latest part of the deal. "Hamas and other factions have confirmed to mediators their readiness to begin implementing the agreement and move to the second phase, provided it receives Israeli approval and that Israel begins implementing the agreement," a Hamas official told AFP on Saturday. Netanyahu met Monday with the Board of Peace's high representative for Gaza, Nickolay Mladenov, who backtracked and said Israel would withdraw only after a full disarmament by Hamas.

items.title: US slams Chinese actions in South China Sea
items.summary: WASHINGTON: The United States on Saturday accused China of "destabilising" activity near the disputed Scarborough Shoal in the South China Sea, saying it is using "dubious" environmental explanations to advance its territorial claims. Scarborough Shoal is a fish-rich reef formation 240 kilometres (124 miles) from the main Philippine island of Luzon and hundreds of kilometres away from mainland China. Beijing claims most of the South China Sea, including the flashpoint shoal, despite an international ruling that its assertion lacks any legal basis.

items.title: Tunku Azizah mourns death of first baby born through her foundation's IVF programme
items.summary: KUANTAN: The first baby born under the Tunku Azizah Fertility Foundation (TAFF) initiative about 20 years ago has died. In a statement posted on the Kesultanan Pahang Facebook page on Saturday, Tengku Ampuan of Pahang Tunku Azizah Aminah Maimunah Iskandariah said Jaden held a special place in TAFF's history. Tunku Azizah, who is also TAFF's founder and lifetime chairman, expressed her sorrow over Jaden's death and described him as her "first grandchild", having been born through in-vitro fertilisation (IVF) treatment with TAFF.

items.title: Kosovo PM egged in parliament as political crisis spirals
items.summary: PRISTINA: Kosovo's parliament had to be suspended on Saturday after an opposition lawmaker pelted caretaker Prime Minister Albin Kurti with eggs, as a long-running political crisis threatens to trigger another snap election. Europe's youngest democracy has faced three elections in less than two years, with successive parliaments collapsing under deep political divisions. Kurti, who has been in days-long negotiations with opposition parties over a new president, attempted to delay a key vote when MP Time Kadrijaj lobbed the yolk-filled projectiles.

items.title: Human Resources Ministry proposes ADTEC JTM-ITE student exchange to strengthen international TVET ties
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Human Resources Ministry has proposed a student exchange programme between Kolej Teknologi Termaju Jabatan Tenaga Manusia (ADTEC JTM) and Singapore's Institute of Technical Education (ITE). Its minister Datuk Seri Ramanan Ramakrishnan said the proposal was raised during his working visit to ITE Singapore as part of the ministry's efforts to strengthen International Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) ties. He said ITE Singapore had welcomed the proposal, paving the way for both sides to finalise details of the collaboration, including student exchanges, knowledge sharing and the sharing of best practices in technical and skills training.

items.title: Camels find unlikely home in outback Australia
items.summary: FAR from their origins in the Arabian desert, hundreds of thousands of camels roam outback Australia where they are used for wild races, an alternative milk source and even to make beer. They're very easily domesticated," he told AFP between camel cuddles. "We haven't met anybody that can't have camel milk," he said.

items.title: Father dies after jumping into pond to save son in Raub
items.summary: KUANTAN: A father's desperate bid to save his young son ended in tragedy today when Mohamed Hafidz Che Din, 46, drowned in a fish pond at a resort in Sungai Ruan, Raub. Raub district police chief Supt Mohd Shahril Abdul Rahman said police received information on the incident at about 3pm. Preliminary investigations found the victim jumped into the pond to rescue his eight‑year‑old son, who had fallen in while trying to retrieve a plastic bread bag used as fishing bait.

items.title: Defence Ministry consistently champions better armed forces structure, career advancement
items.summary: PASIR GUDANG: The Defence Ministry is consistently pushing for improvements to the organisational structure, career progression and allowances of armed forces personnel, its minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said. The move aims to ensure the military's talent management system keeps pace with the modernisation of defence assets and technology. He said detailed proposals covering the three key areas had been submitted to the government and the Public Service Department (PSD) for consideration.

items.title: 15-year-old girl drowns while swimming at Tuaran beach
items.summary: The Sabah Fire and Rescue Department Operations Centre said it received an emergency call at 3.59pm. A search and rescue operation was launched using the Water Surface Searching method around the area where they were last seen. The first victim was rescued, given initial treatment at the scene and later taken to hospital in an Emergency Medical Rescue Services vehicle.

items.title: Gendang 24 Perayaan set for Unesco recognition bid
items.summary: IPOH: Malaysia is moving to elevate Gendang 24 Perayaan onto the world stage, with the Education Ministry set to submit an application for Unesco cultural heritage recognition. Sixteen top primary school teams, comprising 417 students nationwide, competed, showcasing enthusiasm for continuing Malaysia's cultural heritage. Founded in Malaysia in 1988 by the late Tan Hooi Song and Tan Chai Puan, Gendang 24 Perayaan was recognised as Intangible National Heritage in 2009.

items.title: 'Mom, don't call me': Inside Thailand's deadly school shooting
items.summary: Over the next 40 minutes or so, the alleged gunman - another 14-year-old student - ran amok, killing three teachers and two school officials, before turning the gun on himself. GUNMAN TWO DOORS DOWN Trapped inside their classroom in Building 5, Khim started checking messages on her tablet. "I said I knew, and I told her, 'Mom, don't call me, because the ringtone might go off,'" said Khim.

items.title: Israeli settler attacks drive out Palestinian Christians
items.summary: Palestinian Christians call themselves "living stones" due to their communities existence in the Holy Land for the last 2,000 years. Faced with growing uncertainty over economic and security conditions, hundreds of Christians have left since the war in Gaza began nearly three years ago, as attacks by Israeli settlers on Palestinians in the West Bank have become an almost daily occurrence. Between 40,000 and 45,000 Christians are estimated to live in the West Bank, accounting for slightly more than one percent of the population.

items.title: Trump's attack on birthright citizenship faces uphill battle
items.summary: Women "who come here solely for the purpose of giving birth" could get automatic citizenship for their children, Samuel Alito wrote, dissenting from the 6-3 ruling that invalidated President Donald Trump's first attempt to curtail US birthright citizenship. Undeterred by the court's ruling, Trump tried again on Thursday, signing two executive orders largely aimed at birth tourism. "These children are citizens based on their birth on US soil," said University of Virginia law professor Amanda Frost.

items.title: NST Leader: Overqualified, underpaid
items.summary: But low-skilled jobs need strict work permits and higher levies. With starting pay barely supporting an urban lifestyle, desperate graduates are diving into e-hailing jobs, delivering food, packages or driving passengers. Malaysia creates plentiful low-tier retail and administrative jobs but can't generate enough high-paying and high-value tech or corporate jobs.

items.title: Thailand school shooting toll rises to nine after death of 12-year-old girl, police say
items.summary: BANGKOK: The death toll from a school shooting in Thailand rose to nine today after police said a 12-year-old girl who was caught in Friday's incident had died. Police at Plai Bang Police Station in Nonthaburi province told Reuters that the girl died today, a day after a 14-year-old boy allegedly shot his grandparents before killing five people at his school and turning the gun on himself. The suspect, who was also a student, allegedly shot his grandparents before opening fire at Debsirin Nonthaburi School, killing five teachers and staff members on Friday.

items.title: Three men arrested over viral hotel brawl in Johor Baru
items.summary: JOHOR BARU: Police have arrested three men believed to be involved in a fight at a hotel here on Thursday, which was captured in a video that went viral on social media. Johor Baru South district police chief Assistant Commissioner Azrul Hisham Mohd Shaffei said police received information about the incident about 12.55pm today. "Following the information received, police arrested the three men, aged between 35 and 56, in front of the hotel about 3pm today," he said in a statement.

items.title: Six remanded seven days over kidnapping of two foreigners in Alor Star
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Six people arrested to assist in investigations into the kidnapping of two foreigners in Alor Star have been remanded for seven days from today. Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department director Datuk M. Kumar said the suspects comprised a local man, four foreign men and a foreign woman, aged between their 20s and 40s, who were arrested in Kedah, Penang and Kuala Lumpur. Yesterday , two foreigners were shot dead in an exchange of fire with police during an operation to rescue the two kidnapping victims at a house in Taman Amira, Telaga Bata, in Alor Star, about 8.40pm.

items.title: Penang puts ANPR parking enforcement on hold amid public concerns
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN: The Penang government has instructed both local authorities in the state to immediately suspend the implementation of the Automatic Number Plate Recognition (ANPR) system for issuing compounds, pending a review. "The state government will instruct both local authorities, Penang Island City Council (MBPP) and Seberang Perai City Council (MBSP), to immediately suspend the implementation of ANPR and review its details. Chow said the matter was among those discussed during a meeting with Penang DAP chairman Steven Sim and Penang DAP deputy chairman Zairil Khir Johari after he chaired the Penang Pakatan Harapan Leadership Council meeting here today.

items.title: Kelantan police arrest 14,460 in anti drug crackdown
items.summary: Kelantan police chief Datuk Mohd Yusoff Mamat said the arrests, involving 13,950 drug cases, were recorded between January and June. He said the operations were aimed at dismantling drug syndicates, particularly in border districts such as Pasir Mas and Tumpat. Mohd Yusoff said police had also introduced a strategy requiring every district police station chief to make at least one drug-related arrest daily.

items.title: Experts urge holistic measures, warn teacher workload threatens mental health and classroom quality
items.summary: He said the pressure to achieve school performance targets often forces teachers to ‘steal’ breaks until late at night, thus affecting the quality of their personal and family lives. “Some teachers experience emotional stress, fear, and some even experience fatigue or burnout. Meanwhile, Mohammad Faiz said efforts to reduce teachers’ load must be accompanied by concrete and long-term measures, including expanding the appointment of teaching assistants based on school needs and increasing the recruitment of new teachers to fill vacancies.

items.title: Anwar says Malaysia will not be transit route for Israel-bound trade
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has expressed appreciation to the Malaysian Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) for its swift action in seizing a container suspected of carrying strategic goods for export to Israel at the Port of Tanjung Pelepas in Johor yesterday. Earlier, MCBA said it had detained and inspected a container at the Port of Tanjung Pelepas yesterday that was suspected of carrying goods for export to Israel. The agency said the shipment was suspected of violating Item No.

items.title: Highway fight: Police track Perodua driver after viral Ferrari road rage assault [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Police are tracking down the driver of a Perodua Aruz who allegedly assaulted a Ferrari driver during a fight on the North-South Expressway (Plus) that went viral on social media today. Nilai district police chief Superintendent Johari Yahya said police received a report from one of the drivers involved at 6.40pm today. He said preliminary investigations found that the incident occurred around 11am at KM276 of the Plus highway heading towards Seremban.

items.title: Fadhlina hails Nadi Mahir school uniform instalment plan easing parents’ burden, empowering entrepreneurs
items.summary: NIBONG TEBAL, Aug 8 — The National Information Dissemination Centre (Nadi) Mahir initiative, enabling parents to purchase school uniforms on an instalment plan, is helping to ease their financial burden. Elaborating further, Fadhlina said various initiatives implemented through Nadi have directly benefited the community, including the Nadi Tuisyen Rakyat, e-sports, skills training and entrepreneurship programmes. Over 42,000 students nationwide have joined the Nadi Tuisyen Rakyat programme, with more than 73 from Nibong Tebal.

items.title: UAE accuses Iran of targeting ADNOC tanker in Hormuz
items.summary: DUBAI: The United Arab Emirates on Saturday said Iran had targeted a tanker belonging to the state-owned Abu Dhabi National Oil Company (ADNOC) while it was transiting the Strait of Hormuz. Iran has imposed an effective blockade of the strait and wants to charge users for passage, which the US fiercely opposes, and is in talks with nearby Oman over arrangements for the strait's future management. The UAE foreign ministry in a statement condemned what it called a "hostile Iranian attack that targeted a tanker belonging to ADNOC with a missile while it was transiting the Strait of Hormuz, without causing casualties."

items.title: Chow stresses Penang Pakatan unity, BN exco retained as coalition eyes next GE
items.summary: GEORGE TOWN, Aug 8 — Penang Pakatan Harapan (PH) has decided to retain the Barisan Nasional (BN) state executive councillor in the state administration until the next general election (GE), said its chairman Chow Kon Yeow. He said the decision was reached at the Penang PH meeting today based on the electoral pact between PH and BN formed during the 2023 state election. The BN executive councillor is State Rural Development, Agrotechnology and Food Security Committee chairman Datuk Rashidi Zinol.

items.title: Seat swaps possible in Melaka, Zahid says negotiations must remain fair and principled
items.summary: KUDAT, Aug 8 — Barisan Nasional (BN) remains open to negotiations on seat allocations for the Melaka State Election, including seat swaps, provided they are conducted honestly and in good faith, said BN chairman Datuk Seri Ahmad Zahid Hamidi. The Deputy Prime Minister said the basic principle of the negotiations was that seats won by any party must be respected and should not simply be handed over to political partners. “As I have stated, the Melaka Chief Minister (Datuk Seri Ab Rauf Yusoh), who is also the Melaka BN chairman, said that as a matter of principle, in any negotiations, the position of any party that has won a seat must be respected.

items.title: MCKK can re-emerge with revitalised role in modern era, says Sultan Nazrin
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Heritage schools such as the Malay College Kuala Kangsar (MCKK) can re-emerge and take on a revitalised role in the modern era by adapting to the profoundly different context in which they now operate, Sultan of Perak Sultan Nazrin Muizzuddin Shah said today. His Royal Highness said a new approach was needed, one that suited current times while building on the strong ethical and educational foundations that had long defined such schools. Sultan Nazrin, who is Royal Patron of the MCKK Board of Governors, said MCKK and similar schools must adapt and transform in response to new realities, particularly a future shaped by increasingly capable artificial intelligence (AI) and rapid technological change.

items.title: Shrimp import talks with Thailand at final stage, resolution expected by mid‑August, says Mat Sabu
items.summary: KOTA BHARU, Aug 8 — Discussions on the issue of shrimp imports from Thailand are at the final stage and are expected to be resolved by mid-August, said Agriculture and Food Security Minister Datuk Seri Mohamad Sabu. The species are Penaeus esculentus (brown tiger shrimp), Fenneropenaeus merguiensis (banana shrimp), Penaeus vannamei (white shrimp), Penaeus monodon (tiger shrimp) and Penaeus stylirostris (blue shrimp). Mohamad said the Road to MAHA 2026 programme in Kota Bharu was the final instalment after similar programmes were held in Kedah, Selangor, Melaka and Labuan.

items.title: Saifuddin: I was in Sabah when PKR discussed Nurul Izzah's resignation
items.summary: SANDAKAN: Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said he was not present at the party meeting that discussed Nurul Izzah Anwar's decision to resign as PKR deputy president. Saifuddin, who was recently appointed as a PKR vice-president , said he was in Sabah on official duties when the meeting was held yesterday. He was asked to comment on yesterday's PKR Central Leadership Council meeting, which decided to place Nurul Izzah on temporary leave beginning after the 2026 National Congress.

items.title: Container seized at Port of Tanjung Pelepas over suspected Israel-bound shipment [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A container at the Port of Tanjung Pelepas (PTP), Johor, was seized by the Malaysia Border Control and Protection Agency (MCBA) yesterday over suspicions that it contained goods destined for export to Israel. MCBA said the seizure was made following intelligence received by the agency, which then conducted an inspection of the container. MCBA said Malaysia would not compromise on actions that contravened the country's policies, sanctions and laws relating to Israel.

items.title: Perak Education Department vows fair handling of Chemor teacher bullying complaint, welfare prioritised
items.summary: Perak Education, Higher Education, Youth and Sports Committee chairman Datuk Khairudin Abu Hanipah said both parties should adopt a conciliatory approach in resolving the matter instead of blaming each other. “The matter has been brought to my attention, and we have asked the District Education Office and the Perak Education Department to investigate the allegations. Meanwhile, Perak Education director Zulkafli Mohamed Mokhtar said in a statement that the Perak Education Department (JPN) had taken note of the issue which went viral on social media.

items.title: Police seek owner, motive behind pink suitcase left at Bukit Kayu Hitam ICQS after explosive scare
items.summary: ALOR SETAR, Aug 8 — Police have opened an investigation paper to identify the owner and determine why a suitcase was left at the inspection area of the Bukit Kayu Hitam Immigration, Customs, Quarantine and Security Complex (ICQS), after a scan detected images resembling explosives and drugs. Kedah Police chief Datuk Adzli Abu Shah said preliminary investigations found that the spot where the suitcase was left was outside CCTV coverage, making it difficult for police to identify the individual who left it there. Yesterday, police had carried out a process to neutralise a pink suitcase left at the inspection area of the Bukit Kayu Hitam ICQS.

items.title: Amirudin: Selangor govt to meet Panasonic workers over jobs, assistance after planned closure
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Aug 8 — The Selangor state government will meet workers expected to be affected by the closure of television production operations at Panasonic AVC Networks Kuala Lumpur Malaysia Sdn Bhd (PAVCKM) next week to discuss assistance and alternative employment opportunities. Menteri Besar Datuk Seri Amirudin Shari said the meeting would be conducted by State Human Resources, Poverty Alleviation, Indigenous & Minority Affairs Committee chairman V. Papparaidu, together with representatives from the Social Security Organisation (Perkeso), to obtain relevant information from the affected workers. In a statement yesterday, Panasonic Malaysia Sdn Bhd (Panasonic) said production operations for two products would be closed, impacting 400 workers by the end of March next year.

items.title: AADK backs mandatory drug screening for all Malaysia Airlines pilots, cabin crew
items.summary: JERTIH, Aug 8 — The National Anti-Drug Agency (AADK) supports the move by Malaysia Aviation Group (MAG) to make it compulsory for 1,260 Malaysia Airlines (MAS) pilots to undergo drug screening following the recent arrest of one of its pilots in Indonesia. AADK director-general Datuk Ruslin Jusoh said the move to tighten security controls and extend mandatory drug screening to all active pilots and cabin crew members was in line with the zero-tolerance policy towards drug abuse and trafficking. Ruslin said AADK had previously conducted drug abuse detection operations involving flight crew, including at MAS in April 2025 and AirAsia in December 2025.

items.title: Tabung Haji recovery plan addressed RM12.6b losses but further reforms needed, says RCI
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — Lembaga Tabung Haji’s (TH) restructuring and recovery plan successfully restored the institution’s financial position after addressing RM12.6 billion in investment losses, while further reforms are needed to ensure its long-term sustainability, according to the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI). The effectiveness of the recovery measures was reflected in TH’s improved financial performance, with investment income reaching RM4.64 billion last year, its highest since 2018. The commission concluded that the transfer preserved TH’s financial position and described the restructuring and recovery plan as instrumental in resolving the institution’s financial crisis.

items.title: Anwar pledges thorough probe into every Tabung Haji RCI finding following King’s decree
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — The government has pledged to investigate every recommendation thoroughly and the findings in the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), following a decree by His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia. In a Facebook post today, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the move was in line with the Madani government’s commitment to ensuring a comprehensive investigation into the report. “His Majesty’s order for a thorough investigation into the RCI report reflects the Madani government’s commitment to ensuring that every recommendation and finding is fully investigated without compromise,” he said.

items.title: MACC, police and IRB ramp up investigations into alleged Tabung Haji irregularities after RCI report
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — Enforcement agencies have stepped up action following the release of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) report on Lembaga Tabung Haji (TH), with investigations now focusing on individuals linked to alleged management irregularities at the institution. By yesterday, the Malaysian Anti-Corruption Commission (MACC) had remanded five individuals to assist in investigations into various alleged misconduct uncovered in the 211-page report released on July 29. Following severe asset impairment, the report recommended forensic audits into several high-risk investment decisions involving PT TH Indo Plantations, Emrail Sdn Bhd, Wellspring Worldwide Limited, Abraj Sdn Bhd, Putrajaya Perdana Bhd, TH Plantations Bhd, TH Properties Sdn Bhd, Alam Maritim Resources/TH Marine, TH Hotel & Residences Sdn Bhd and FGV Bhd, which allegedly resulted in substantial losses to depositors’ funds.

items.title: Malaysia’s interfaith approach offers lessons for peace, social harmony, says Aaron
items.summary: MELAKA, Aug 8 — Malaysia’s experience in managing religious, cultural and ethnic diversity can offer valuable lessons to the international community in advancing interfaith understanding, peace and social harmony, Minister of National Unity Datuk Aaron Ago Dagang said. Speaking at the International Interfaith Peace Conference (IIPC) 2026 here today, Aaron said interfaith dialogue had an important role in strengthening mutual understanding and building a more cohesive society. Instead, interfaith dialogue is about creating mutual understanding while respecting our differences,” he said.

items.title: Two killed in separate Perak accidents involving lorry, three vehicles and family car
items.summary: IPOH, Aug 8 — Two people were killed in separate accidents, one near the West Coast Expressway (WCE) toll plaza near Teluk Intan and the other at Kampung Pulau Juar near Kampung Gajah. Perak Fire and Rescue Department assistant director (Operations) Sabarodzi Nor Ahmad said the Teluk Intan accident today involved a 25-tonne empty lorry and two vehicles, a Toyota Vellfire and a Honda HRV. “A 50-year-old man in the Honda HRV suffered minor injuries, while the 31-year-old lorry driver escaped unhurt,” he said in a statement today.

items.title: IRB urged to probe possible tax evasion involving Tabung Haji group, subsidiaries
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — The Inland Revenue Board (IRB) should look into possible tax evasion involving the Tabung Haji group and its subsidiaries as investigations intensify following the findings of the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) for the 2014-2020 period. The advisor to the Enforcement Focus Group at the Enforcement Agency Integrity Commission (EAIC) Prof Datuk Mazlan Ahmad said a comprehensive investigation should also be supported by forensic accounting to trace the flow of funds, including their origin, destination and beneficiaries. Therefore, IRB must look into this,” he said in an interview on The Nation programme aired by Bernama TV.

items.title: Gobind urges fail‑safe layers, says unchecked AI could jeopardise trust and national security
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Aug 8 — Safety and security assessments must precede the adoption and deployment of new technologies to prevent operational failures and safeguard user reliance, said Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo. Speaking at the MyMahir Artificial Intelligence (AI) Roadshow here today, Gobind highlighted a previous high-profile AI event launch that encountered technical glitches involving an autonomous robot, which provided crucial lessons on technological readiness and security controls. “Actually, we must ensure that it (AI) is safe before we use it.

items.title: Pulau Redang must be protected, Terengganu mulls heavier penalties for violating boat operators
items.summary: KUALA TERENGGANU, Aug 8 — The state government will hold an engagement session with tourism operators and relevant agencies to discuss the issue of coral reef damage believed to have been caused by anchoring activities in prohibited areas. Razali said the state government would also study proposals to review permits for day-trip operations or impose heavier penalties on boat operators who flout the rules. He said the state government would not compromise with any day-trip operators or boat operators found to have ignored the stipulated operating procedures, resulting in damage to coral reefs.

items.title: DOE confirms haze movement, unhealthy API hits Serian, Kuching, Samarahan, Sri Aman, Bintulu
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Aug 8 — Air quality in the country has worsened, with five areas in Sarawak recording unhealthy Air Pollutant Index (API) readings as of 8am today. Department of Environment (DOE) deputy director-general (Development) Azuri Azizah Saedon said the five areas with unhealthy API are Serian (171), Kuching (154), Samarahan (154), Sri Aman (139) and Bintulu (124). She also said that three areas recorded good air quality while 60 areas recorded moderate readings.

items.title: Saifuddin Nasution vows stronger security, aims to place Malaysia in Global Peace Index top 10
items.summary: SANDAKAN, Aug 8 — Malaysia is aiming to achieve a position within the top 10 of the Global Peace Index as Malaysia is currently ranked 12 out of 165 countries. Home Minister Datuk Seri Saifuddin Nasution Ismail said within Asean, Malaysia ranked second behind Singapore and third in the Asia-Pacific region below Singapore and New Zealand. Saifuddin Nasution said, a review of these advisories would not only acknowledge Malaysia’s security achievements, but would also strengthen confidence, encourage tourism, promote sustainable investment and further deepen the longstanding friendship between Malaysia and respective countries.

items.title: King orders tighter airport security, urges ministries to curb drug smuggling nationwide
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — His Majesty Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia today called on the relevant ministries and agencies to tighten security controls and enhance security measures at all country’s airports and entry points. In a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar’s Facebook page, His Majesty said the measures were important to curb drug smuggling and prevent cross-border criminal activities that could threaten public safety and order. “Security at the country’s entry points must always be strengthened through more effective enforcement, continuous monitoring and close cooperation among all relevant agencies,” he said.

items.title: King orders thorough probe into Tabung Haji RCI report, says guilty parties must face action
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — His Majesty, Sultan Ibrahim, King of Malaysia today decreed that the investigation into the Royal Commission of Inquiry (RCI) Report on the Tabung Haji (TH) Board be carried out exhaustively. In a post on Sultan Ibrahim Sultan Iskandar’s official Facebook, His Majesty said that the move is important to ensure that all parties responsible are appropriately dealt with, as well as to ensure that the same thing does not happen again in the future. In addition, Sultan Ibrahim also said that the investigation into the matter should be carried out comprehensively, without compromising on any party found guilty.

items.title: Fahmi: Constituency allocations at PM’s discretion, funds should go directly to people
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — The special constituency allocation is at the discretion of the Prime Minister, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today, amid controversy over several PKR MPs losing access to the MyKhas portal. Fahmi said the allocation was not a personal entitlement of MPs and that the Prime Minister had the prerogative to determine how the funds were channelled for the benefit of constituents. He said the mechanism announced by Anwar would see allocations for MPs managed through the Prime Minister’s political office.

items.title: Fahmi: AI cannot replace human moderators in detecting cyberbullying, Tamil language a case in point
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — Artificial intelligence (AI) cannot be left entirely in charge of moderating online content as it may fail to understand the nuances of certain languages, particularly when dealing with cyberbullying, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. He said this was particularly evident in cases involving cyberbullying within the Tamil-speaking community, where AI-based moderation could fail to properly identify harmful or abusive content. He said the two codes were intended to ensure social media platforms did not become hubs for crimes including scams, cyberbullying and other offences.

items.title: Nurul Izzah remains party member, Anwar has full backing of govt parties, says Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — The resignation of Nurul Izzah Anwar from her party leadership post will not affect her commitment to PKR, Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said today. Fahmi said Nurul Izzah remained a party member and would continue to support its struggle, while stressing that component parties remained committed to supporting Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. He said Nurul Izzah had resigned and requested time to focus on her PhD studies, with the party’s leadership responsibilities to continue under its existing leadership structure.

items.title: Police corporal killed in Sabah electrocution laid to rest as family recalls final video call
items.summary: His eldest sister, 34-year-old Nurlella Rahim, said her family expressed their appreciation to the Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) for assisting in facilitating the arrangements to bring her brother’s remains home. Nurlella said the five siblings were very close and often made video calls almost every day, including through the family WhatsApp group. “We made video calls with each other almost every day.

items.title: Police neutralise unattended luggage at Bukit Kayu Hitam ICQS complex, no explosives found
items.summary: Kubang Pasu police chief Supt Mohd Radzi Abdul Rahim said the pink luggage was found at about 5.55 pm after no one came forward to claim it. “The luggage was then taken for scanning and Customs personnel found images indicating the possible presence of suspected drugs and explosive materials. “The luggage was opened at 11 pm, and no explosive materials were found.

items.title: Police kill two suspects in shootout during Alor Setar kidnap rescue operation
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — Two suspects, believed to be foreigners, were killed in a shootout with police during an operation to rescue two kidnap victims at a house in Taman Amira, Telaga Bata, Alor Setar, Kedah, last night. Bukit Aman Criminal Investigation Department (CID) director Datuk M. Kumar said the incident occurred at about 8.40 pm when the suspects fired several shots at the Special Investigation Division (D9) team from the Bukit Aman CID. Kumar said police also found a Beretta semi-automatic pistol loaded with five rounds of ammunition, a revolver containing four rounds of ammunition and a long machete near the two suspects.

items.title: Education minister challenges vocational students to use drones to improve school security
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — Students of Setapak Vocational College have been challenged to develop innovative ways of using drone technology to enhance security on their school campus. Education Minister Fadhlina Sidek said the students had been given one month to study and identify the best ways to apply the technology before presenting their proposals to her. “Within a month, I want the students to present to me how drone technology can be used to help improve school security,” she said in a Facebook post yesterday.

items.title: Malaysia, Cambodia strengthen defence ties, cooperation in AI and drone technology
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Aug 8 — Malaysia and Cambodia are committed to further strengthening bilateral ties, particularly in defence and security, while contributing to Asean’s collective resilience. Defence Minister Datuk Seri Mohamed Khaled Nordin said the commitment was expressed during his courtesy call on Cambodian Prime Minister Samdech Thipadei Hun Manet at the Peace Palace in Phnom Penh yesterday. He said Malaysia and Cambodia are also committed to strengthening defence cooperation in new areas, including jungle warfare training, the defence industry, artificial intelligence (AI) and drone technology.
